cohort: The study included 1243 women giving birth (617 vaginally, 626 via C-section) at seven hospitals in seven different regions of China.
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with higher mean breast milk concentrations of iron, copper, zinc, and manganese compared to C-sections, with the difference in copper concentration being statistically significant.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with higher breast milk concentrations of essential trace elements (iron, copper, zinc, and manganese) than C-sections, with only copper concentrations showing a statistically significant difference.
